messages.subject: WASO
parts:
Hi guys,

Has anyone tried to calculate WASO from the sleep variables in Part 5 summary? If anyone has used them, how do you describe the night-wake variables associated with accelerometry parameters? The common description for MOD and VIG activity assumes there has been 100-400 or >400 mins of activity. Lastly, what is a good real life example of an activity that requires 30 mg? Not very many activity categories use miligravity as a unit. 

Thanks
Sharmin

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] WASO
parts:
Shouldn't that be: Total of all time use categories related to the night minus total sleep duration within the sleep period time window?
You do not need to discriminate between inactivity, moderate and vigorous activity for this. I would sum them and treat them together as wakefulness after sleep onset..
Needless to say that with wakefulness we actually mean 'more acceleration then in sleep', because an accelerometer does not directly measure the underlying neurological process of sleep and wake.
Vincent
